Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Insurance Group Q3 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. Instructions for queuing your questions will be provided at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex Insurance Group's Q3 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are Michael Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer; David Patel, Chief Underwriting Officer; Robert Kline, Chief Investment Officer; and Elena Vasquez, Chief Operating Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we are making today may be considered forward-looking. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause our actual results to differ materially from those projected. We encourage you to review our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks and uncertainties.

I will now turn the call over to Michael Reynolds.

Michael Reynolds: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on Apex Insurance Group's performance for Q3. We delivered strong results, driven by the positive impact of our pricing discipline on premium volume growth, solid realized and unrealized gains and losses in our investment portfolio, favorable changes in our actuarial assumptions, robust new business production volumes, improving customer acquisition cost trends, and effective management of total catastrophe losses. We are particularly excited about the initial success of our ApexDrive UBI program and its strong contribution to retention and risk selection across personal lines.

Lisa, our CFO, will now provide a more detailed review of our financial performance.

Lisa Chen: Thank you, Michael. Good morning, everyone. As Michael mentioned, we had a solid quarter. Our net income was $850 million, or $2.45 per share. Key drivers of our financial performance included disciplined pricing actions boosting premiums, strong investment returns, actuarial favorability, new business momentum, CAC efficiencies, and contained cat impacts despite elevated activity. Our combined ratio was 93.2%. Investment income for the quarter was $450 million, reflecting strong performance in our fixed income and alternatives segments. We continue to maintain a strong capital position, with surplus at $22 billion and an RBC ratio of 520%.

Let me dive deeper into some of these highlights, starting with the impact of our pricing changes on premium volume, which was a major top-line driver. In this hardening P&C market, marked by ongoing inflation in repair costs, medical expenses, and reinsurance pricing, we've stuck to a rigorous approach to rate adequacy in both personal and commercial lines. This delivered robust premium growth while protecting margins. Specifically, consolidated gross written premiums grew 9.2% year-over-year to $14.8 billion in Q3, with net earned premiums up 8.7% to $12.1 billion. This extends our streak to the 11th straight quarter of double-digit earned premium growth in core U.S. personal lines. Pricing changes drove about 65% of this, equating to a 6.1% booked rate increase portfolio-wide, with the rest from organic volume, retention, and new business.

By line, personal auto faced sharp loss ratio pressures from 12% higher claim severities due to parts inflation and labor shortages, so we rolled out average renewal rate hikes of 9.8%. Leveraging our proprietary generalized linear models enhanced by telematics from ApexDrive, now on 2.8 million policies, we tailored pricing by risk tier—safe drivers got 4-5% increases, high-risk up to 15%. Premium volume rose 11.4% to $5.2 billion, beating elasticity norms in this mature market, with retention climbing to 89.2%, up 120 basis points year-over-year. Our 7% UBI attach rate outpaced competitors like Progressive and Geico, who saw softer retention with broader hikes.

In homeowners and dwelling fire, against a $25 billion cat year-to-date from California wildfires and Southeast storms, we actioned 7.5% average increases, targeting high-exposure states like Florida and Texas. Premiums jumped 13.2% to $4.1 billion, with losses moderated by our reinsurance tower renewal at 15% higher cession rates. Policy count still grew 2.1% via cross-sell with smart home IoT partners, similar to Allstate's plays. This helped our combined ratio improve 180 basis points to 92.4%, creating a virtuous cycle of price, volume, and profitability.

Commercial lines, 35% of the book, saw 5.2% average rate gains—above the 4.1% industry average per AM Best—with workers' comp up 6.8% amid OSHA trends, driving 7.9% growth to $3.4 billion. Our AI risk selection engine flagged 15% more adverse risks pre-bind, growing exposure units 4% without quality dilution.

Regionally, the U.S. led with 78% of momentum and 12.1% growth from rate actions in fire and hurricane zones. Europe was flat at 2.3% or €2.1 billion, limited by Solvency II and UK motor caps to 3.5% hikes, though Nordic motor grew 8% digitally. Asia-Pacific hit 14% growth to A$1.2 billion, leveraging 8-10% property increases post-floods in Indonesia and Australia.

This discipline rests on key initiatives: our ApexPrice 2.0 platform with satellite imagery, Verisk cat analytics, and real-time elasticity testing showing -0.4 in auto versus historical -1.2; expanded behavioral pricing via telematics cutting adverse selection 22%; and portfolio tweaks like non-renewing $450 million in underperforming California HO-3 risks, shifting to Midwest for 1.5 points net volume lift. We see pricing adding 5-7% to FY24 growth, with Q4 indications at 7.2%. Retention targets 92%, new business CAGR 10%, supporting 15% ROE expansion.

Next, on new business production volume, we posted $15.2 billion in total new business premiums, up 12% year-over-year on an annualized premium equivalent basis, our ninth straight double-digit quarter. Policy count hit 2.1 million, up 8%. P&C took 66% at $10.0 billion, up 18%, with commercial P&C soaring 25% to $4.2 billion on cyber and D&O demand post-ransomware like Change Healthcare. Our CrowdStrike-partnered cyber scoring improved quote-to-bind 15%, adding $850 million. Personal P&C grew 12% to $5.8 billion, auto new business up 22% via DriveSafe telematics with gamification, hitting 28% digital conversions.

Life and annuities were $3.1 billion, flat with discipline amid high rates; IUL up 9% to $1.2 billion on 5.3% Treasury yields, whole life modest versus Northwestern Mutual pressure; 450,000 policies, up 5% via agents and RIAs.

Group health and specialty added $2.1 billion, up 15%, 650,000 policies up 12%, led by 30% uptake in voluntary benefits and stop-loss, plus $250 million parametric expat product with AXA.

North America was 62% at $9.4 billion, up 14%, from California reforms and Florida stability. Europe $2.5 billion, up 7%, motor/SME in UK/Germany with 35% telematics. Asia-Pacific $2.0 billion, up 22%, life in India HDFC Ergo JV, health micro with Grab/Gojek (180,000 policies). Latin America $1.3 billion, up 10%.

Digital/embedded now 42% of new business, up from 32%, via Amazon/Shopify APIs; $150 million YTD tech spend cut manual reviews 40%, loss ratios under 92%. VNB margin up 200 bps to 18.5% via reinsurance. Cats like Helene tempered personal, competition cyber led to ceding fleet auto. FY guide 11-13%, Q4 parametric ag product $500 million; 2025 pipeline $65 billion.

Customer acquisition costs also improved sharply. Blended CAC fell 12% year-over-year to $218 per new policy, fourth straight sequential drop, trailing 12-month average $235 below $250 target, beating S&P's $290 industry. Direct digital, 58% of P&C new, at $142 CAC down 18%, versus agent $345 flat. Marketing as % of new premium to 9.2% from 11.8%, via ML attribution on Google Analytics/Snowflake, cutting low-intent spend 35%, high-LTV focus, 3.2x ROAS on Trade Desk.

Embedded with Uber/Lyft: 15,000 policies at $89 CAC, 95% instant via telematics. SecureLife Flex wearables: 8% life new at $165, 40% underwriting cut.

North America $210 down 10%, softer ads but CA reinsurance nudge. EMEA $245 down 14%, UK open-banking like Aviva, Germany bundles 4.2x LTV. APAC $198 up 5% QoQ on entry, but Grab/Gojek micro at $75; blockchain KYC pilots.

LTV/CAC to 4.8x from 3.9x, P&C 5.2x. AI personalization predicts churn, +22% leads; OEM like Ford targets 20% auto sub-$100; cross-sell amortizes CAC in 9 months. Prioritize commercial (CAC $410, 7.1x LTV). Q4 to $200, 2024 $50M martech for sub-$220.

On catastrophe losses, they totaled $1.45 billion pre-tax, 7.8% of Q3 GWP, versus $1.12 billion or 6.2% last year, Q2 $850 million or 4.9%. YTD $3.67 billion, 6.5% of GWP, up from 5.1%. GWP up 12% to $18.6 billion on rates/retention. Elevated from SCS (1,200+ tornadoes/hail NOAA), CA fires, Europe windstorms; secondary perils now 40% U.S. PML per RMS/AIR.

North America 65% or $940 million (9.2% regional GWP): $620 million Midwest/Southeast auto/home net of $410 million reinsurance; CA $210 million commercial. Europe 22% $320 million (6.1%): Ciarán/floods $280 million U.K./Germany, +$40 million prior favorable. APAC/other 13% $190 million (4.8%): Yagi/Japan $150 million, parametrics $45 million efficient.

Ex-cats, loss ratio to 61.2% up 180 bps; cats hit combined 420 points vs. 300 target. AI/Guidewire/Verisk improved reserves 15%; 2023 reinsurance higher attachments ($1.5B U.S. wind), $750M cat bonds at 5.75%. Duck Creek algorithms cut hurricane GPML 22%; ILWs $2.3B above $20B industry. Q4 4-5% GWP, stress-tested AR6; diversify E&S +25%, parametrics 8% new, M&A cyber/liab. Rates 10-12% 2024, RAROC 15%+.

Finally, changes in actuarial assumptions drove a $285 million favorable impact, 15% of $1.9 billion adjusted operating income, versus $120 million headwind last year; YTD $650 million toward $800-900 million guide. Mortality/longevity: $180 million in group life/annuity (42% $450B book), mortality down 12 bps ages 60-80 U.S. term per SOA/2.5M data, longevity +0.3 years UK PRT; $2.1B reserve release, EV +4% to $28B, IFRS 17 $450M CSM. Lapses up 150 bps UL/VUL $120B on inflation/unemployment, $65 million favorable with NLG floors. Discount rates +45 bps to 4.6% Treasury/spreads, $28 million P&C to 4.8% yields, Solvency II to 205%. Morbidity +8 bps health $12 million headwind on mental claims +22%.

U.S. 65% reserves dominant; Europe PRT/L&G $40M, MA €15B +7%; APAC Japan lapses offset Australia health. Actuarial Modernization/Milliman/AWS ML +18% mortality accuracy, RMS v18.1 cat AAL +5% $30B home, IFRS 17 PAA volatility -25%. RBC 520% >400%, $1.2B buybacks; PRT/FIA growth, $5B UK pipeline 1% longevity; dynamic hedging 95%.

These elements combined for our strong quarter. David, over to you for underwriting.

David Patel: Thank you, Lisa. I'd like to provide an update on our underwriting performance. We've seen continued strong performance in our personal auto and homeowners lines. We are actively managing our exposure to catastrophe risks and secondary perils, and have implemented several initiatives to improve our risk selection, including AI-powered engines, telematics integration via ApexDrive, and dynamic pricing algorithms that have reduced GPML exposure significantly while growing premiums.

Robert Kline: Thank you. From an investment perspective, we have continued to focus on diversifying our portfolio and managing risk in the current market environment. We are seeing positive returns from our investments in investment-grade fixed income, corporates, Treasuries, MBS, and alternatives like direct lending and real estate. Our $152 billion general account portfolio is 72% investment-grade fixed income—45% corporates, 20% U.S. Treasuries and agencies, 7% MBS—15% equities in S&P 500 and blue-chips, 13% alternatives.

Realized gains netted $265 million, up 28% from last year, beating $220 million guide. Opportunistic sales of $1.8 billion intermediate corporates (4.2-5.1% yields, utilities/financials like JPM/Duke) locked 2.1% returns post-Fed pause; $45 million equity from tech trim amid volatility, avoiding drawdowns. Losses $18 million energy cyclicals at $75 oil, offset; YTD $612 million +15%, duration to 5.8 years from 6.4, reinvest at 4.8% vs. 3.9%.

Unrealized losses $1.47 billion, up $320 million QoQ on 4.35% 10-year Treasury amid inflation/Fed; fixed $1.62 billion (85% corporates/MBS, spreads -12 bps, rates +25 bps); equities +$152 million on S&P 8% rally financials/staples. U.S. 82% bore 22% QoQ expansion; Europe €12B milder $180 million (ECB dovish 2.4% Bunds, 5.2% sterling); APAC 6% +$45 million JGBs/Aussie.

ALM/BlackRock Aladdin flags munis >5.5% tax-equivalent; $4.2B new at 4.9%, swaps hedge $2.5B duration to 0.3 years gap; 18% new ESG green/sustainability. Q3 gains $240-280 million, stress 50 bps shift; supports 12.4% ROE, M&A dry powder like MetLife.

Elena Vasquez: Just to add briefly, our operations teams have been key in executing these strategies, with digital platforms driving efficiencies across distribution and claims.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: Thank you. Instructions for questions: Please press star then one. Our first question comes from John Ramirez with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Ramirez: Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of pricing changes on premium volume and elasticity?

Michael Reynolds: Good morning, John. Happy to expand. As Lisa detailed, our 6.1% booked increases drove 65% of growth, with auto at 9.8% tailored hikes yielding 11.4% volume despite pressures—elasticity at -0.4 thanks to segmentation. Homeowners 7.5% added 13.2%, policy growth via cross-sell. This balance keeps us ahead.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Carter with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter: Good morning. Could you discuss the impact of elevated catastrophe activity on your business?

Lisa Chen: Good morning, Emily. Cats at 7.8% of GWP were a headwind, but ex-cats loss ratio improved to 61.2%. Proactive reinsurance, cat bonds, and portfolio steering limited net impact, with underlying discipline shining. Q4 expected milder at 4-5%.

Operator: Our next question comes from David Lee with Barclays. Please go ahead.

David Lee: What is the expected impact of IFRS 17 and Solvency II changes on your underwriting strategy?

David Patel: Good morning, David. These standards sharpen our focus on BEL, CSM, and risk adjustment. We've adapted with PAA for P&C reducing volatility 25%, MA growth in Europe, and ML models for assumptions. Positions us for PRT/FIA growth without capital strain.

Operator: Our next question from Sarah Kim with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Sarah Kim: On new business and CAC—how sustainable is the double-digit growth with CAC declines?

Lisa Chen: Sarah, very sustainable. Digital shift to 58%, embedded at sub-$100 CAC, ML attribution boosting ROAS—all while VNB margins hit 18.5%. LTV/CAC 4.8x, flywheel from cross-sell. Guide holds 11-13% FY.

Operator: Our final question from Mike Thompson with Deutsche Bank. Thoughts on actuarial favorability persisting?

Lisa Chen: Mike, yes—$285 million this quarter from credible mortality normalization, lapses, discounts. Tech like AWS/ML ensures quarterly recalibration; YTD $650 million toward guide. Embedded edge for ROE.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time.

Michael Reynolds: Thank you for your questions and your interest in Apex Insurance Group. In closing, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering strong results and creating value for our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
